key_insight: A unified crystal plasticity-fracture model shows that creep cracking shifts from trans-granular at high stress to inter-granular at low stress, driven by the competition between slip-induced intragranular cracking and grain-boundary cavitation.
engineering_relevance: This mechanistic map links micro-scale crack evolution to macroscopic creep rupture ductility and life, helping engineers predict whether a component will fail in a more ductile or quasi-brittle manner under service stress.
method: Explicit polycrystalline microstructure with crystal plasticity.
Grain-boundary cavitation coupled with crystallographic crack propagation.
Stress-dependent simulations resolving crack-path transitions and damage localization.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports microscale computations across stress levels that reproduce distinct cracking regimes and quantify their impact on rupture ductility and creep life.
watch_item: The framework is computational and mechanism-focused, so predictive accuracy will depend on calibration of grain-boundary and fracture parameters for the specific alloy and loading condition.
paper_title: Mechanistic transition between inter- and trans-granular creep cracking via a unified crystal plasticity-fracture framework
